```{r}
#| label: setup
library(ringtest)
library(tidyverse)
```

Import the demonstration data included in the `ringtest` package and make a quick visualization of the data.

```{r}
data("ringtest_demo")

ggplot(ringtest_demo, aes(level, value, color = lab)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge())

ggplot(ringtest_demo, aes(level, value, color = lab)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge()) +
  facet_wrap(~ level, nrow = 1, scales = "free")
```

Calculate cell statistics and Mandel's $h$ and $k$ statistics. Compare against critical values. The ISO norm specifies these are only indicatory and no decisions should be made based on these statistics alone.

```{r}
mhcrit <- mandel_h_indicator(p = 10, alpha = 0.05)
mkcrit <- mandel_k_indicator(p = 10, n = 5, alpha = 0.05)

cellstats <- calc_cell_stats(ringtest_demo) |> 
  calc_mandel_hk() |> 
  mutate(
    ksign = ifelse(k < mkcrit, 0, 1),
    hsign = ifelse(abs(h) < mhcrit, 0, 1)
  )

ggplot(cellstats, aes(level, h, fill = factor(hsign))) +
  facet_wrap(~ lab, nrow = 2) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge()) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(1, -1) * mhcrit, lty = 2) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

ggplot(cellstats, aes(level, k, fill = factor(ksign))) +
  facet_wrap(~ lab, nrow = 2) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge()) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mkcrit, lty = 2) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

Formal statistical tests for outliers should be done with Cochran's test for outlying variance and Grubb's test for outlying means (single & double).

```{r}
outliers <- test_outliers(cellstats)
outliers |> 
  filter(!is.na(coalesce(cochran, grubbs_single, grubbs_double)))

# this should be an interactive proces: examine the outliers and decide what to do with them, here we just remove the respective data
ringtest_demo_clean <- ringtest_demo |> 
  filter(
    !(lab == "Lab_08" & level == "Level_2"),
    !(lab == "Lab_10" & level == "Level_5")
  )
```

Calculate the precision statistics per level. This is applied on the cleaned dataset. The following plot shows the reproducibility variance for each level and the distribution of its two components (repeatability variance and inter-laboratory variance):

$$
\sigma_R^2 = \sigma_r^2 + \sigma_L^2
$$

```{r}
precision_tbl <- precision(ringtest_demo_clean)

# plot of variance components
precision_tbl |> 
  pivot_longer(c(s_r, s_L), names_to = "varcomp", values_to = "sigma") |> 
  mutate(
    sigma2 = sigma^2,
    varcomp = factor(varcomp, c("s_r", "s_L"), 
                     c("repeatability", "inter-laboratory"))
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(m_hat, sigma2, fill = varcomp)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * sigma2 / s_R^2)), 
                position = position_stack(.5), size = 3) +
  labs(fill = "variance component", y = "reproducibility variance",
       x = "level")
```

The different types of relationships described in the ISO reference are fitted on the precision estimates.

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\text{0})\ s &= A \quad \text{(constant)} \\
(\text{I})\ s &= bm \\
(\text{II})\ s &= a + bm \\
(\text{III})\ s^2 &= a_v^2 + (b_vm)^2 \\
(\text{IV})\ s &= Cm^d \\
\end{aligned}
$$

```{r}
# reproducibility
fit0 <- with(precision_tbl, fit_precision_relationship(m_hat, s_R, rel = "0"))
fit1 <- with(precision_tbl, fit_precision_relationship(m_hat, s_R, rel = "I"))
fit2 <- with(precision_tbl, fit_precision_relationship(m_hat, s_R, rel = "II"))
fit3 <- with(precision_tbl, fit_precision_relationship(m_hat, s_R, rel = "III"))
fit4 <- with(precision_tbl, fit_precision_relationship(m_hat, s_R, rel = "IV"))

ggplot(precision_tbl, aes(m_hat, s_R)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  geom_line(aes(y = fit0$fitted, color = fit0$rel)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = fit1$fitted, color = fit1$rel)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = fit2$fitted, color = fit2$rel)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = fit3$fitted, color = fit3$rel)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = fit4$fitted, color = fit4$rel)) +
  labs(title = "Reproducibility", color = "Type of relationship (ISO)")

# repeatability
fit0 <- with(precision_tbl, fit_precision_relationship(m_hat, s_r, rel = "0"))
fit1 <- with(precision_tbl, fit_precision_relationship(m_hat, s_r, rel = "I"))
fit2 <- with(precision_tbl, fit_precision_relationship(m_hat, s_r, rel = "II"))
fit3 <- with(precision_tbl, fit_precision_relationship(m_hat, s_r, rel = "III"))
fit4 <- with(precision_tbl, fit_precision_relationship(m_hat, s_r, rel = "IV"))

ggplot(precision_tbl, aes(m_hat, s_r)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  geom_line(aes(y = fit0$fitted, color = fit0$rel)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = fit1$fitted, color = fit1$rel)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = fit2$fitted, color = fit2$rel)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = fit3$fitted, color = fit3$rel)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = fit4$fitted, color = fit4$rel)) +
  labs(title = "Repeatability", color = "Type of relationship (ISO)")
```
